content: This medication should be used as a foam applied rectally, following your doctor’s instructions. Typically, it is used in the morning and evening for the first two weeks, then once daily in the evening for the next four weeks. Since this medication is flammable, avoid smoking while applying it and immediately afterward. It is best to use this medication after a bowel movement. You may apply it while standing, lying down, or sitting. Do not insert any part of the canister into the anus; instead, use the enclosed applicator. Follow the instructions provided to attach the applicator to the canister. Before use, warm the canister in your hands and shake it well for 10 to 15 seconds. Hold the canister upside down, gently insert the applicator tip into the anus, and press down on the pump, holding it in place for two seconds to release the foam. Afterward, release the pump and keep the applicator in place for 10 to 15 seconds before removing it. Dispose of the applicator after use and wash your hands thoroughly. If you are taking another corticosteroid orally (e.g., prednisone), do not stop taking it unless directed by your doctor. Abruptly stopping corticosteroids can worsen certain conditions, such as asthma or allergies, and may cause withdrawal symptoms like weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, or dizziness. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication when starting budesonide. Notify your doctor or pharmacist immediately if you experience withdrawal symptoms. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase the dose, use it more frequently, or continue it longer than prescribed. Do not stop using this medication without consulting your doctor, as some conditions may worsen if the drug is stopped suddenly. Nausea may occur as a side effect. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, potentially causing side effects associated with excessive corticosteroid levels. These effects are more likely in children or individuals using the medication long-term. Budesonide may also reduce your ability to fight infections, increasing the risk of serious (rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations. In rare cases, long-term use of corticosteroids may temporarily slow a child’s growth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, and the risks and benefits should be discussed with your doctor. Babies born to mothers who have used corticosteroids long-term may develop hormone-related issues. This medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (81–162 mg daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. In case of overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, consider lifestyle changes such as weight-bearing exercise, ensuring adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, quitting smoking, and limiting alcohol consumption. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
